I agree with all three points, and checking approval safety against the real input path turned up a genuine gap. The status is now labelled as you suggested: **implementation self-assessment passed; independent acceptance pending**.

**Approval safety.** Commit `83e7405` had a real gap. The 400 ms grace period was the only guard, and it started when the approval arrived rather than when the panel was first drawn. Keys already queued in the terminal relied on that timer alone. A burst of keys was fed in one at a time, so `yyy` typed 0.8 s after the panel appeared approved the action. A test in a pseudo-terminal against a `83e7405` build showed the sidecar receiving `approve`. Bracketed paste was already safe.

The fix is commit `804c5df`:
- No decision is accepted before the panel has been drawn, and the grace period starts at that first frame.
- Input already queued when an approval opens is discarded.
- Sidecar messages that arrived while waiting for input are applied before that input.
- A burst of several keys never answers an approval.

The new terminal test `tui_approval_input_e2e`:
- **Setup:** it freezes the TUI while the approval arrives and `y⏎` is typed, then resumes it after the grace period.
- **Inputs that must not decide:** the queued keys, a delayed `yyy` burst and a bracketed paste of `y⏎`. None of them decides.
- **Deliberate keys:** a single `n` denies (the file isn't written), and a single `y` approves (it is).
- **Results:** 3 of 3 runs pass on `804c5df`, and it fails against `83e7405`.

One behaviour remains by design and is disclosed (O6): text typed while the agent works, before any panel exists, is sent as steering and shown in the transcript. If the TUI stalls, whether such input lands before or after the approval depends on thread timing. It never decides an approval.

**Narrowed scope.** These are now explicit open items instead of "all rows pass":
- O1: live budget information is not shown.
- O2: the session id is not in the status bar.
- O3: resumed history leaves out earlier tool activity.

O4–O6 are disclosed limitations: Markdown nesting and reflow, durations timed by the TUI's own clock, and the steering behaviour above.

**Verification by revision.** The report now has a table of which checks ran on which build. The one that matters most: a full `make build` and `make test` from a clean checkout of `804c5df` gave Rust 237/237, CLI 728/728 (including all four terminal scenarios), and clean security gates. The visual evidence is still from `83e7405`. `804c5df` changes only how approval input is handled and adds its own test.

**Runtime state.** The report and my project memory both record that the installed `nexus` runs the build in `~/nexus-code`. That checkout is on the unmerged branch `feat/tui-surface`, built at `804c5df` (`nexus-tui` hash starts `c56080de`). Dogfooding on this host since about 06:50 UTC has used the branch build, not main.

The commits are `804c5df` (fix) and `696178a` (report). Nothing is merged, pushed or published.

The read-only review you describe should be done by someone other than me, since I wrote the code. It should cover `804c5df` as well as `83e7405`, with the evidence in `docs/reviews/evidence/tui_surface/` and the new approval test.

input.description: Peer harness comparison research
input.prompt:
You are researching current, primary-source facts about peer coding harnesses for a qualification assessment of Nexus Code (a local-inference-first coding agent harness with a TS CLI/sidecar, Rust engine and Ratatui TUI at /home/mike/nexus-code). Read /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/RULES.md first (read-only rules apply; you will mostly use the web).

Peers: OpenAI Codex CLI, Anthropic Claude Code, and 2-3 relevant open-source harnesses (choose among OpenCode/sst, Aider, OpenHands, Goose, Crush — prefer those with real local-model support and a terminal UI). Use only primary sources (official docs, official repos/READMEs/CHANGELOGs, release notes, official blog posts); record the URL and the date/version you saw for every fact. Today is 2026-10-12; prefer the most recent docs/releases and note version numbers.

For each peer, collect DOCUMENTED capabilities (say "documented" — do not claim measured performance) relevant to these areas:
1. Objective completion: planning/todo tracking, plan mode, verification/test-running behaviour, how "done" is decided.
2. Context/long tasks: automatic compaction/summarisation, manual compaction, context-window handling, session save/resume/fork, memory files.
3. Tools/execution: file edit model (diff/patch/search-replace), shell execution, timeouts, background processes, parallel tool calls, subagents/delegation, git integration/undo/checkpoints.
4. Operator control/trust: approval modes, sandboxing (OS-level: seatbelt/landlock/containers), network restrictions, read-only modes, workspace boundaries, secrets handling, MCP/plugin trust, hooks.
5. Inference compatibility: local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoints), provider list, tool-calling requirements, retries/failover, context-limit handling, token/cost accounting.
6. Terminal experience: TUI features (markdown, diffs, approvals UI, keybindings, themes, IDE integration).
7. Persistence/auditability: transcripts, session files, exportable logs, telemetry/OTel.
8. Product delivery: install methods, supported platforms, update mechanism, signing/provenance/SBOM if documented, license, release cadence, security policy/vulnerability reporting.
9. Evaluation: any published benchmark claims (e.g. SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench) — record exactly what is claimed, by whom, with which model; mark these as vendor claims, not verified.

Also find 1-2 primary sources for widely used agent evaluation suites (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench or similar) describing what they measure, so the assessment can define a matched evaluation.

Deliver /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/peers.md containing: a comparison table (rows = areas above, columns = peers) with short documented facts and citation keys; a citation list (key → URL, title, date/version accessed); a section "Behavioural reference points for Nexus" listing concrete behaviours peers document that a top-tier harness is expected to offer (phrased as testable behaviours, not architectures to copy); and a "Limitations" section (what you could not verify, paywalled/unavailable sources). Never present a vendor benchmark as measured parity evidence. Keep it under ~400 lines.

input.description: Tools, execution, persistence review
input.prompt:
You are an independent reviewer assessing Nexus Code's tool/execution quality and persistence/auditability. Read /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/RULES.md first and follow it strictly (read-only; isolated extracts; exact citations; finding format).

Architecture: TS CLI/agent in cli/src (agent.ts tool loop, tools.ts, core/operation_runner.ts, core/state.ts durable task state, core/persistence_protection.ts, session.ts, session_export.ts, evidence.ts, file_diff.ts, checkpoint.ts, sandbox.ts, mcp.ts, plugins.ts), Rust engine core/src (main.rs RPC/`call`, file_ops.rs, search.rs, shell/exec code, cst.rs), bridge between them. Review main (3727938) primarily; note differences on feat/tui-surface (696178a) and fix/context-convergence (31d6622) where relevant (`git diff main <branch> -- <path>`).

Area 3 — Tool and execution quality. Assess actual correctness and failure semantics:
- File operations: write/edit/patch/delete semantics, atomicity (temp+rename? fsync?), partial mutation on failure (e.g. multi-replacement edits failing midway, patch partially applied), behaviour when the file changed concurrently between read and edit (stale-content detection?), encoding/CRLF/BOM/no-final-newline preservation, symlink handling, large files, binary files.
- Diffs: per-operation diff accuracy (file_diff.ts) incl. concurrent external changes during an edit.
- Search tools (search_code, list_dir, find_files): gitignore handling, output bounds, truncation disclosure.
- Shell execution (run_command, run_tests, background processes): timeouts, output bounds and truncation markers, process-group cleanup on timeout/cancel (orphans?), cancellation latency, environment/secret leakage, working directory enforcement, interactive commands hanging.
- Parallel tool execution (agent.ts read-only parallel path) and delegation (spawn_subagent): isolation, concurrent writes, result integrity.
Do isolated deterministic reproductions where cheap: e.g. build the engine in an extract and use `harness-core -w <tmp> call --tool <tool> --args '<json>'` to probe edit failures, concurrent modification, timeouts (`run_command` with sleep + timeout), process cleanup (spawn a child that ignores SIGTERM and check for orphans with ps), output bounds. Use the mock gateway only if you need the agent loop.

Area 7 — Persistence and auditability: state schemas and versioning/migration (core/state.ts, session.ts), compatibility with older session files, atomic writes and crash recovery (kill mid-write?), exports (session_export.ts; nexus-session-export/2), event chronology, tool-call identity (stable ids call_<sha>), receipts and evidence ledger, milestone duplication, stale verification (verifier attempts keyed by inputs fingerprint — can a verifier pass be reused after the deliverable changed?), and whether authoritative state and user-facing summaries (TUI banner, export, receipt) agree. Look for existing tests before declaring gaps (grep cli/test and core tests).

Deliver /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/tools_persistence.md: findings in the required format (priorities, labels, exact citations, reproduction commands and output), a short "what is solid" section with evidence, Checks actually run, Limitations.

input.description: Trust boundaries and inference review
input.prompt:
You are an independent reviewer assessing Nexus Code's operator control/trust boundaries and inference compatibility/recovery. Read /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/RULES.md first and follow it strictly (read-only; isolated extracts; exact citations; finding format). Never call a real inference endpoint; use the mock gateway (cli/test/helpers/fixtures.ts startGateway, which can return tools/text/http replies, delays and chunked streams) or a tiny local HTTP server you write in your temp dir for malformed responses.

Review main (3727938) primarily, noting differences on feat/tui-surface (696178a, the installed runtime) and fix/context-convergence (31d6622).

Area 4 — Operator control and trust. Review the real enforcement paths, not only handlers:
- Approvals/review mode: which tools require approval, can any mutating path bypass it (MCP tools, plugins, subagents, run_tests, git tools, patch_file, background processes, `!command`, slash commands that mutate)? Check cli/src/core/authority*.ts, agent.ts confirm paths, sidecar.ts requestApproval, repl.ts.
- Read-only mode (`--read-only`/config.readOnly): enforced for every mutating tool, shell commands and MCP? Find gaps by tracing each tool's dispatch.
- Workspace boundaries: path resolution in Rust (file_ops.rs canonicalisation, symlinks, `..`, absolute paths), TS editTarget, shell cwd; filesystem races (TOCTOU between check and write).
- Explicit scope acceptance (objective ledger: only operator can accept descoping) — can the model mark requirements verified/descoped improperly?
- Secrets: redaction coverage (ui.ts redactSecrets, redact.rs), what is sent to model destinations (env vars, file contents, .env files read by tools), where secrets are persisted (sessions, audit logs, inference receipts, diffs).
- Model destinations: which endpoints receive what (planner/coder models, subagents, embeddings, web search), whether a misconfigured endpoint can exfiltrate workspace data, TLS handling (any rejectUnauthorized=false?).
- Plugin/MCP trust: plugins auto-loaded from ~/.nexus/plugins and other dirs (code execution at startup?), MCP servers started from config, permission prompts.
- Steering races and queued input at the sidecar protocol level (dedupe, ordering).

Area 5 — Inference compatibility and recovery (local inference first-class): provider adapters (cli/src/client.ts, providers.ts, protocols/), streaming SSE parsing (partial lines, multi-byte splits, [DONE], usage chunks), tool-call parsing (OpenAI tool_calls deltas, malformed JSON arguments, text-embedded tool calls from local models, parser.ts), empty replies, provider errors (429/503/timeouts) and retries/backoff, execution ambiguity (a tool call executed when the stream later failed? duplicate execution after retry?), failover, context-limit handling (capacity admission, provider 400 context errors), and resource accounting (provider-reported vs estimated usage, inference receipts). Build small deterministic reproductions against the mock/your own server for: malformed tool-call JSON, a stream cut mid-tool-call, an empty assistant message, a 503 then success, a reply with a tool call embedded in text (local-model style), a context-length 400 error. Run them through the real agent loop in an isolated extract (e.g. a tiny tsx script or a node:test file in your extract using ApplicationCore/SidecarServer like cli/test/sidecar_surface.test.ts does). Record observed behaviour precisely.

Deliver /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/b0de2c87-d169-4fb3-8dbd-05906b5022a2/scratchpad/assess/trust_inference.md: findings in the required format, a short "what is solid" section with evidence, Checks actually run, Limitations.

All commands run read-only against /home/mike/nexus-code or in an isolated extract of 696178a
(`scratchpad/assess/x696178a`, built with `npm run build` and `cargo build --release`).

### A1 A wrong deliverable ends VERIFIED and its requirement `verified`
- Priority: P0 · Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT · Affects: main, feat/tui-surface (installed runtime); fix/context-convergence (same verifier model, see its gating changes 8674520/cb3e20f/547525b — gating by configured verifier does not bind to the deliverable either)
- Trigger: objective "1. add math.js exporting add(a, b) that returns a + b"; the model writes `exports.add = (a, b) => a - b;`, runs the discovered verifier, marks R1 verified, calls task_completed. The repository suite (`npm test`) passes but never exercises math.js.
- Expected: not VERIFIED (no evidence covers the deliverable); R1 at most `implemented`.
- Observed: `{"execution":"COMPLETED","outcome":"VERIFIED","verifier":"npm test","R1":"verified","file":"exports.add = (a, b) => a - b;"}` (repro `scratchpad/assess/repro_false_verified.test.ts`, run in the 696178a extract).
- Cause (source): the verifier is the first generic command found in the repository — `cli/src/tester.ts:77-104` (`make test`, `cargo test`, `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test`); `verified` on a requirement needs only some passing verifier attempt recorded on the current workspace — `cli/src/core/objective.ts:335-340` (main 3727938, unchanged on 696178a). Nothing relates the run to the changed files or to the requirement text. Turn VERIFIED derives from verifier evidence status alone — `cli/src/agent.ts` outcome derivation (`evidence?.status === "PASSED"` → VERIFIED; see the block around lines 3436-3470 on main).
- Impact: VERIFIED — the strongest claim Nexus makes — can be printed for incorrect work whenever the repository's suite is green and does not cover the change. This is the common case for new features.
- Remediation: separate "suite passed" from "deliverable verified". (1) Record per-requirement acceptance checks: operator-supplied commands/tests, or model-proposed checks the operator accepts (`/requirements` UI); (2) require fail-before/pass-after evidence for new checks (run against the pre-change checkpoint); (3) require that a passing run touched the changed files (coverage or test-file selection) before VERIFIED; otherwise report `COMPLETED · tests passed, deliverable unverified`. Keep the generic suite as a regression gate (REGRESSION_FREE), not as verification.
- Acceptance test: the repro above must end not VERIFIED and R1 not `verified`; a variant where the operator-accepted check `node -e "assert(require('./math').add(2,3)===5)"` exists must fail on the wrong implementation and pass on the correct one; mutation suite (10 seeded wrong deliverables with green unrelated suites) → 0 VERIFIED.
- Dependencies: objective ledger (main), checkpoint snapshots (main). Not addressed by unmerged work.

### D1 Build identity is not observable; the installed runtime silently follows the checkout
- Priority: P1 · Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT · Affects: installed runtime (all branches)
- Trigger: the checkout is on unmerged feat/tui-surface @ 696178a; run `nexus --version` and `nexus doctor --json`.
- Expected: version output and doctor name the commit, branch/tag and dirty state of the running build, and warn when it is not a release or not main.
- Observed: `nexus --version` → `1.2.1`; doctor `install.build` evidence `['version 1.2.1', 'install root /home/mike/nexus-code']`, `nexusVersion 1.2.1` — identical to main. `cli/src/doctor.ts` has no git/commit lookup (grep for rev-parse/gitHead/commit: no matches). `/usr/local/bin/nexus -> /home/mike/nexus-code/harness.sh` runs `core/target/release/nexus-tui` and `cli/dist` from the working tree (`harness.sh:14-43`).
- Impact: dogfooding results, bug reports and evidence cannot be attributed to a build; a branch switch in the dev checkout changes what users run with no signal (exactly the current state).
- Remediation: generate build info at build time (commit, describe, dirty flag, build time) into `cli/dist/build-info.json` and Rust `env!` via build.rs for harness-core and nexus-tui; print it in `--version`, the doctor (`install.identity` finding: warn when dirty or not on a release tag/main, fail when the three components disagree), the TUI status line or receipt, session exports and inference receipts.

- Dependencies: none.

- Observed: no `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` or other pipeline definition in the repository root (checked `ls -a`); `git remote -v` is empty. `make test` (Makefile:47-50) is the only gate and is run manually.
- Impact: merges to main are not gated; regressions depend on the implementer remembering to run the suite; results are not reproducible by others.
- Remediation: a pipeline (the operator runs a self-hosted GitLab) running `make build`, `make test` (incl. PTY scenarios, which need only a pty, no display) and the security gates on every branch, required for merges to main; artefacts: test logs, build-info, SBOM.
- Acceptance test: a deliberately failing test on a branch blocks its merge request; pipeline logs show commit identity.

### D3 Installation is the development checkout; no versioned install, upgrade or rollback
- Priority: P1 · Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK · Affects: installed runtime
- Observed: README documents building in place; `harness.sh` resolves its own directory and executes the working tree's artefacts; the version is a constant 1.2.1 in `cli/package.json` and `package.json`; no `make install`, packaging, tags or release notes (no CHANGELOG).
- Impact: upgrade = git pull + rebuild in the tree that is also being developed; rollback = git checkout + rebuild; a half-finished build or a test run that rebuilds artefacts changes the live runtime.
- Remediation: `make install PREFIX=~/.local` copying a built, identified release into `<prefix>/lib/nexus/<version-sha>/` and switching a `current` symlink (rollback = switch back); release tags with notes; the launcher refuses to mix components from different builds.
- Acceptance test: install release A, then B, then roll back to A with one command; `nexus --version` reflects each; rebuilding the dev checkout does not change the installed runtime.

### D4 Supply-chain and policy files missing or partial
- Priority: P2 · Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Observed: `package.json` declares `"license": "MIT"` but there is no LICENSE file; no SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting process; no CHANGELOG. `make verify-reproducibility` (Makefile:36-45) only rebuilds the TypeScript CLI twice (Rust artefacts not checked; fixed /tmp paths). Security gates run npm audit and cargo audit and a pattern secret scan (`scripts/security_gates.sh:26-127`); `scripts/generate_sbom.sh` writes a CycloneDX-style SBOM to `dist/` but nothing signs artefacts or records provenance.
- Remediation: add LICENSE, SECURITY.md (contact, supported versions, response targets), CHANGELOG; extend reproducibility to the Rust binaries (`--locked`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, path remapping) and compare hashes across two clean builds; attach SBOM + checksums to tagged releases; optional signing.
- Acceptance test: two clean builds of a tag on different directories produce identical hashes for all three components; SBOM lists Rust and Node dependencies with versions.

### D5 Repository hygiene: a session transcript and personal paths are tracked
- Priority: P3 · Label: REPRODUCED (source)
- Observed: `nexus-session-session_20261011_162349_6lvu.json` (124 KB conversation export, 13 `/home/<user>/` paths, no credential-shaped strings) is tracked in the repository root, added by a9437ba (an earlier "land outstanding changes" commit made by the assessing agent's own session); README hard-codes `/home/mike/nexus-code/cli/.env` (README.md:182).
- Remediation: move session exports out of the tree (export into `.nexus/exports/`, gitignored), remove the tracked file, make README paths relative.

### D6 Platform scope
- Priority: P2 (product scope) · Label: PRODUCT IMPROVEMENT
- Observed: README.md:3 states Linux; doctor repairs use `/proc/self/fd` (`cli/src/safe_fs.ts`); the TUI relies on unix process groups. Peers document macOS and (for most) Windows/WSL support.
- Remediation: declare Linux-only support explicitly in docs and doctor; if macOS is targeted, replace /proc-based checks with fcntl(F_GETPATH)/fstat comparisons and run CI on macOS.

### P1 Fixed per-request overhead is large and unmeasured against task outcomes
- Priority: P2 · Label: EVIDENCE GAP (measurement) · Affects: all
- Observed (estimate): the first request of the installed build carries 38 tool schemas (incl. 5 browser tools, LSP, CST, trigram/hybrid search) = 17,784 chars plus a 2,342-char system prompt; whole body 20,383 chars ≈ 5.1k tokens at 4 chars/token (estimate, not provider-reported; repro `repro_overhead.test.ts`). Measured (provider-reported, earlier this session with `scripts/token_accounting.py`): the 2026-10-11 dogfood session used 2,506,632 prompt tokens over 87 requests (≈28.8k per request), exactly the sum of provider usage reports.
- Impact: on local inference, fixed overhead and repeated full-context resends dominate latency and context headroom; no data shows which tools are used or what the overhead costs in task success.
- Remediation: measure first (per-request breakdown: system, tools, pinned objective, history, tool results); then admit tool groups by need (browser/LSP/CST only when enabled or requested), and report per-request token composition in receipts.
- Acceptance test: receipts carry a composition breakdown; on the evaluation set, the reduced tool set keeps task success within noise while lowering median prompt tokens per request (pre-registered threshold).

### E1 No matched task-level evaluation exists
- Priority: P1 · Label: EVIDENCE GAP · Affects: all
- Observed: 55 CLI test files (deterministic mock gateway, harness behaviour) and Rust unit tests; dogfood campaign reports (docs/reviews/*DOGFOOD*); one controlled experiment (`experiments/context-validation-2026-10-04/RESULTS.md:52-53`: "n = 4 per cell; … one model; one task family"). No maintained suite that runs fixed coding tasks against fixed repositories and scores artefact correctness; no SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench-style runner (grep found mentions only in planning docs).
- Impact: completion rate, correctness and recovery are unproven; mechanism changes (compaction, continuation) are judged by individual dogfood runs.
- Remediation: see the evaluation plan in the main report (fixed repos/commits, hidden acceptance tests, fault injection, matched settings, separate scores).

## Positive evidence (checked)
- Token accounting is provider-reported where available and reconciles exactly (2026-10-11: sum of reported usage over 87 requests = session tokenStats).
- Doctor: 18 pass / 0 fail on the installed runtime (`nexus doctor --json`, inference check skipped); repairs are symlink-safe (reviewed earlier, safe_fs.ts).
- Security gates exist and distinguish scanner failure from findings (scripts/security_gates.sh:26-99).

## Checks actually run
- `git status/branch/log/worktree list/remote -v`, `ls -l /usr/local/bin/nexus`, sha256 of runtime artefacts — identity recorded in the main report.
- `ps` for running nexus processes — none.
- `git -C /home/mike/nexus-code archive 696178a | tar -x` → npm run build (0), cargo build --release (0).

## Limitations

- Token figures for overhead are character estimates.

It has 16 tool/execution findings (T1–T16) and 6 persistence findings (P1–P6), plus "What is solid", "Checks actually run" and "Limitations". I ran everything on main 3727938 in my own extract (`assess/tp/main`). Neither branch changes the tool-layer files (`file_ops.rs`, `runner.rs`, `main.rs`, `tools.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `tester.ts`), so the tool findings should apply to feat/tui-surface, fix/context-convergence and the installed runtime too. I judged that from the diff only and did not rerun the probes on those branches.

**P1 findings I reproduced:**
- **T1 – edits land on the wrong text:** `edit_file` falls back to a fuzzy match at 85% similarity. A snippet naming a line that doesn't exist (`check_permissions(a)`) succeeded and deleted the real `audit_log(a)` line, with no sign that a fuzzy match happened.
- **T2 – wrong match edited:** when the snippet appears more than once, only the first copy is replaced, but the result says `replacements: 2`.
- **T3 – unsafe writes:** `edit_file` and `write_file` overwrite in place, with no temp file and no fsync, and nothing checks whether the file changed since the model read it. The fallback rewrites every CRLF in the file to LF. `write_file` always reports `overwritten`, even for a new file.
- **T4 – `patch_file` damages files:** it overwrites any existing `<name>.tmp_patch` file, drops the executable bit, replaces a symlink with a regular file, strips CRLF, and applies each hunk at the first matching context.
- **T6 – lost tool requests:** shell commands inherit the engine daemon's stdin, which carries the queued tool requests. A `cat` command swallowed a queued `write_file` request, which never ran and never got a reply.
- **T11 – `run_tests` filter injection:**
  - The `filter` argument is pasted unescaped into a shell command; a probe filter created a file.
  - The command goes through no approval prompt.
  - `run_tests` is treated as read-only, so it runs in parallel with other tools.
  - A trailing `echo` can make a failing suite count as a passed verification.
- **P1 – persistence failures are silent:** every durable write is wrapped in an empty catch. With the state directory made read-only, a turn modified the workspace while the saved state stayed at 0 messages, with no warning anywhere.

**Lower-priority findings I reproduced:**
- **T7:** after the shell exits, the timeout no longer applies, so background children keep the call open (8 s against a 3 s timeout).
- **T8:** the engine panics when output over 32 KB is cut through a multi-byte character, so a command that ran shows as failed.
- **T10:** commands inherit the full environment. The `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY` value and passwords in DB URLs reach the provider; only `sk-`-style keys are masked.
- **T13:** dry-run actually executes commands that look read-only, such as `echo x > file`.
- **T15:** `list_dir`, `file_tree` and `cst_symbols` can list paths outside the workspace (`/etc/ssh` worked).
- **T16:** search results are silently capped at 50 with no "truncated" flag, and a single match can return a 200 KB line.
- **P2:** every `update_plan` call records all completed phases as new milestones again.
- **P3:** the state file is written mode 664, without fsync, and with no lock against a second writer.

**Found by reading the code, not reproduced:**
- **T14 (P1):** subagents run in the same workspace without approval prompts, and their edits don't demote requirements already marked verified.
- **T5:** `delete_file` removes whole directories with no approval prompt.
- **T12:** the parallel path skips the cancellation check, and the engine has no way to cancel a running command.
- **T9:** command output is buffered in memory without limit before it is truncated.
- **P4:** only one in-flight operation is recorded, so a crash during a parallel batch under-reports.
- **P5:** resuming by session id uses a substring match, and every load error is reported as "not found".
- **P6:** fix/context-convergence adds a `findings` field without a schema version bump and drops the on-disk full diffs.

**What held up:** timeouts kill the whole process group (a child ignoring SIGTERM was gone; PTY mode too). Command output truncation is clearly marked. The working directory and file descriptors are confined to the workspace. `patch_file` changes nothing unless every hunk matches. Per-operation diffs are accurate. State saves are atomic, loading fails closed on corrupt or future-version files, and older files are migrated, all covered by existing tests. ## 1. Executive verdict

**Nexus is not yet a top-tier coding harness, and its maturity on representative coding objectives is unmeasured.**

What it is qualified for today (with evidence):
- **Supervised, single-operator use on trusted repositories** where the operator reads every change: the agent loop,
  continuation budgets, objective ledger, steering, per-operation diffs, provider recovery (429/503, stream resets
  without duplicate tool execution) and the TUI work as designed in deterministic tests and reproductions.
- **Read-only analysis**: `--read-only` is enforced by an allowlist plus a read-only bubblewrap sandbox; a write
  attempted through a test script changed nothing (`trust_inference.md`, "what is solid").
- **Diagnostics**: `nexus doctor` (18 checks, symlink-safe repairs) and exact, provider-reported token accounting.

What remains unproven:
- Completion rate and artifact correctness on representative tasks (no matched evaluation exists, E1).
- Long-task reliability with local inference after compaction (the context branch has no accepted run, CTX-05).
- Supportability for anyone but the developer on this host (no CI, no versioned install, no build identity).

What blocks top-tier status (all reproduced unless noted):
1. **Execution boundaries can be bypassed in review mode** (P0): `delete_file "."` deleted the workspace including
   `.git` without approval (T-01); subagents run every tool unapproved (T-02); `run_tests.filter` is shell-injected and
   ungated (T-06/T11); opening a cloned repository executes its plugins and MCP servers without a trust prompt, even
   with `--read-only --approve` (T-03).
2. **VERIFIED can be printed for wrong work** (P0): a deliberately wrong implementation ended `COMPLETED/VERIFIED`
   with its requirement `verified`, because the verifier is any green generic suite (A1; also CTX-03, T-09).
3. **Tools and the parser can change the wrong thing** (P1): `edit_file`'s silent fuzzy fallback deleted code the
   model never named (T1) and edits only the first of several matches while reporting all (T2); `patch_file` drops the
   executable bit, replaces symlinks and strips CRLF (T4); tool calls inside `<think>` reasoning are executed — a
   deletion the model explicitly declined was performed (I-01); JSON repair rewrites Python file content (I-02); a
   shell command can swallow queued engine requests (T6).
4. **Secrets leave the boundary or persist in plaintext** (P1): `batch_read` returns `.env` (T-05); a quarantined
   secret was rehydrated into a `search_web` query (T-07); common secret formats reach the model and durable stores
   (T-08, T10).
5. **Approval input in the TUI is not safe against ordinary typing** (P1): typing across the panel's appearance
   approves, and the `a` in "add" granted "approve all later actions" (F1); approvals replace open panels so keys meant
   for them decide (F3) — on the installed build and on main.
6. **No evidence base for qualification**: no task-level evaluation (E1), no CI (D2), no build identity (D1).

Passing suites (Rust 237, CLI 728 at 804c5df), VERIFIED outcomes and self-assessed acceptance do not change this
verdict: the defects above all sit in paths those suites do not exercise.

## 3. Qualification standard

A top-tier harness, for this assessment, must meet all of:

| ID | Criterion | Observable test |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Completes representative coding objectives reliably | pass rate on a matched task set (fixed repos, hidden acceptance tests, ≥5 runs/task) at or above a pre-registered threshold |
| Q2 | Produces correct changes and reports outcomes truthfully | artifact correctness by hidden tests; false-VERIFIED rate 0 on a mutation set; tools never change unintended text |
| Q3 | Preserves operator intent and evidence through long tasks | constraints and facts introduced early are honoured/retained after compaction, resume and continuation; no false absence claims |
| Q4 | Enforces trustworthy execution boundaries | every mutating/egress capability gated by mode and context; untrusted workspaces cannot execute code; secrets never leave or persist in plaintext |
| Q5 | Provides a usable, safe terminal experience | independent visual acceptance; approvals cannot be decided by stray input; keyboard-only, narrow/short terminals, escaping |
| Q6 | Recovers from failures | provider faults, context-limit errors, crashes and resume end in a correct state or a truthful bounded failure |
| Q7 | Ships as a supportable product | identified, reproducible, versioned builds; CI; install/upgrade/rollback; docs that match behaviour; vulnerability process |
| Q8 | Treats local inference as first-class | the above hold with local OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama) including their error/streaming shapes |

## 5. Peer reference (documented capabilities, not measured parity)

From `peers.md` (primary sources, versions as of 2026-10-12): Codex CLI 0.162.1, Claude Code 2.1.296, OpenCode 1.19.0,
Goose 1.54.0, Aider 0.86.2. Behaviours peers document that Nexus lacks or does differently, phrased as tests:

- **OS-level sandboxing of commands** (Codex, Claude Code: Seatbelt/bubblewrap; network allowlists). Nexus sandboxes
  only in read-only mode; review mode is an approval list with bypasses (Q4).
- **Workspace trust before executing project configuration** (Claude Code and Codex document trust prompts for
  project-scoped settings/hooks/MCP). Nexus auto-loads workspace plugins and MCP servers (T-03).
- **Local backends with context-window sizing** (Aider sizes Ollama `num_ctx` per request; Goose warns about silent
  truncation). Nexus has capacity admission but no reactive handling of provider context errors (I-05).
- **Interrupted-tool awareness on resume** (Claude Code marks cut-off tool calls for the model to check). Nexus records
  in-flight operations in a single slot (P4) and the context branch loses mid-turn findings on crash (CTX-01).
- **Checkpoints/rewind with documented limits** (Claude Code rewind excludes shell-made changes). Nexus has checkpoints
  and `/undo`; its limits for shell changes are documented for diffs only.
- **Release discipline**: Codex and Claude Code ship signed/packaged releases several times a week with changelogs;
  Nexus has none of these (Q7).
- Claude Code documents no support for non-Claude models; it cannot be a matched local-inference comparator. Codex
  (`--oss`, built-in Ollama/LM Studio providers; Responses wire format), OpenCode, Goose and Aider can be.
- Benchmark figures found are vendor claims about models under other harnesses; none establishes harness parity.

**Verdict:** Nexus is not a top-tier harness yet, and its success rate on real coding tasks is unmeasured. Four safety boundaries can be bypassed, VERIFIED can be printed for wrong work, and some tools can change the wrong thing.

The report is `docs/reviews/NEXUS_TOP_TIER_QUALIFICATION_ASSESSMENT_2026-10-12.md` (SHA-256 `5313945030b7…`). The five specialist reviews and the reproduction scripts are in `docs/reviews/evidence/qualification_2026-10-12/`. All are untracked and nothing was committed; the branch, the installed runtime and the configuration are unchanged.

**What it's qualified for today:**
- **Supervised use on trusted repositories**, by an operator who reads every change.
- **Read-only analysis.** `--read-only` held under test: a test script that tried to write changed nothing.
- **Diagnostics:** `nexus doctor`, and exact token accounting from provider-reported usage.

**What blocks top-tier status.** All of these were reproduced on both main and the installed branch build:
- **Approval bypasses in review mode:**
  - `delete_file "."` deleted the repository, including `.git`, without asking.
  - Subagents run every tool without approval.
  - The `run_tests` filter allows command injection.
  - Opening a cloned repo runs its plugins and MCP servers with no trust prompt, even with `--read-only --approve`.
- **False VERIFIED:** a deliberately wrong `add` (it returned `a - b`) ended VERIFIED, because any green test suite counts as verification.
- **Wrong edits:**
  - `edit_file` silently fuzzy-matched and deleted a line the model never named.
  - `patch_file` drops the executable bit and replaces symlinks.
  - A tool call written inside the model's `<think>` reasoning was executed, deleting a file the model said it would not delete.
- **Secrets:** `.env` contents reach the model through `batch_read`, and several secret formats are stored in plaintext.
- **TUI approval input** (independent review, overturning my earlier "PASS"): typing across the panel can approve. The `a` in "add" granted "approve all later actions".
- **No evidence base:** no task-level evaluation, no CI, and no build identity. `nexus --version` prints only `1.2.1`, so nothing shows that the installed runtime is an unmerged branch.

**Context-convergence branch:** it merges cleanly but is not acceptable. Its only real test run produced no artifact, and the new findings store loses findings after a crash. One defect affects main as well: operator steering beyond the last 10 messages, or past 600 characters, disappears after compaction.

**The report also contains:**
- the qualification standard (eight criteria) and a matrix showing evidence and gaps per criterion
- a peer comparison (Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenCode, Goose, Aider) using documented capabilities only, with no parity claims
- a backlog of 8 acceptance blockers, 11 reliability items and the polish list
- a 10-stage implementation sequence with measurable exit criteria
- an evaluation plan covering tiers, fixed run conditions, separate scores, proposed thresholds, and local versus cloud setups
- an evidence manifest

The independent TUI review gave the visuals "accepted with defects" and did not accept approval input. Its reproductions of the approval problems were unit-level, not real keystrokes in a terminal.

**Limitations:**
- **No live inference:** model behaviour was scripted, so the report shows what Nexus accepts, not how often a real model triggers it.
- **Peers not run:** the peer facts come from documentation.
- **Independence:** I implemented the TUI work under review; a separate agent reviewed that part.

**One action for you:** a reviewer's probe printed a real API key from its shell environment into that agent's local transcript. It isn't in any report file (I checked by value), but I'd rotate that key.

content.text:
Four groups of work remain before `feat/tui-surface` can be merged. They come from the independent TUI review and the branch's own open items. The approval-input fix (`804c5df`) holds for what it targeted (queued keys, bursts, pastes, Ctrl+C, a sidecar crash), but the review found three cases it doesn't cover.

**1. Approval input (blocks merge)**
- **F1, P1: typing across the panel approves.** If you're mid-sentence when the approval panel opens, each `y`/`a`/`n`/Enter after the 400 ms grace period counts as a decision. In the review's test, the `a` in "please add tests" granted "approve all later actions". Default focus is Approve, so Enter approves too.
  - Fix: no decision keys while you're still typing, default focus Deny or none, and Enter only after an explicit focus move.
- **F3, P2: an approval replaces whatever panel is open.** If help, the diff review, the model picker or the connect panel is open, a key meant for that panel decides the approval. Partially typed connect input is lost.
  - Fix: queue the approval behind the open panel, with a visible notice.
- **F2, P2: decisions below 40×10.** The panel counts as shown even when only "needs a larger terminal" is displayed, so `y` approves an unseen change. At exactly 40×10 the panel shows no diff rows.

**2. Test reliability**
- **F5:** the terminal tests fail when run in parallel. The surface scenario lost a `/resume` submission in 2 of 8 runs under load. The cause isn't established, so a real lost keypress can't be ruled out.
  - Fix: run the terminal tests one at a time, and wait on sidecar acknowledgements instead of sleeps.

**3. Open items O1–O3**
- **O1:** a live budget display (step n of 300, time left). This needs a new field in the sidecar's activity event.
- **O2:** the session id in the status bar. The dirty-file count `●3` also has no label.
- **O3:** resumed history shows only text, not earlier tool calls or outcomes.

**4. Visual defects (mostly P3)**
- **Approval panel:** about 25 empty rows between a one-line diff and the buttons, and the wording "Nexus wants to: creates config.json". At 40 columns the buttons wrap and the kind line is cut without an ellipsis.
- **Cancelled-turn screen:** the change card is drawn before its "approved" line.
- **Code blocks:** a wrapped code row loses the block's background.
- **Command preview:** it shows the first 6 lines and hides the last one, which is often the informative one. A tail preview would suit commands better.
- **Help:** cut off with no scroll indicator.
- **Crash screen:** it still says "(no exit code)" after naming the signal, and its only diagnostic line is stale, left over from an earlier cancelled turn.
- **At 40 columns:** the status bar drops the review-mode indicator, and the activity line is cut without an ellipsis.
- **Narrow diffs:** wrapped rows restart at the line-number column and break mid-word.
- **Evidence gap:** the diff screenshots date from before the surface work and were never re-captured on the shipped build.

**Exit criteria for merging**
- F1–F3 are fixed, with a terminal test of continuous typing across the panel opening.
- The terminal tests pass repeatedly (for example 10 runs), including under load.
- O1–O3 are either implemented or explicitly accepted by you as deferred.
- The evidence is re-captured from the final commit, and a reviewer other than me signs off on the visuals again.

The larger blockers from the assessment are not specific to this branch and exist on main too: the review-mode bypasses, workspace trust, false VERIFIED, edit correctness and secrets. They belong in their own branches, starting with the single execution authority (Stage 1), so they don't hold up this one.

79	
80	### F1 Ordinary typing that continues across the approval panel's appearance approves, including "approve all later actions"
81	- Priority: P1 (bypasses the review-mode safety gate; the consequence is session-wide auto-approval)
82	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT (unit level, real state machine)
83	- Affects: main, feat/tui-surface, installed runtime
84	- Trigger: In review mode the operator is typing (e.g. a steering message, at human speed of about 150 ms per key)
85	  when an approval request arrives. Keys stay single events (no burst), so after the 400 ms grace each `y`, `a`, `n`
86	  or Enter is a decision.
87	- Expected: Typing that was already in progress when the panel appeared never decides. "Approve all later actions"
88	  needs a deliberate, confirmed act.
89	- Observed: 804c5df:core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs:1156-1160 maps Enter→focused (default Approved,
90	  :812-822 `focus: Verdict::Approved`), `y`→Approved, `a`→ApprovedForSession, `n`/Esc→Denied. The only time guard is
91	  :1168-1172 (`APPROVAL_GRACE` = 400 ms, :342). I added a test in the extract
92	  (`live_state::tests::review_human_typing_across_the_panel_decides`). It submits a turn, types "ple", applies the
93	  approval, marks it shown at t0, then feeds "ase add tests" at t0+150 ms·k. Output:
94	  `first decision: Some((4, 'a', Send(Approve { id: "approval-1", always: true })))`: the `a` of "add" approved
95	  every later action. Letters before it were silently swallowed (`scroll_overlay`). main (live_state.rs:1011-1020)
96	  has the same mapping, with the grace counted from event receipt.
97	- Impact: Review mode can be turned into auto mode by a common English letter. The action and all later ones run
98	  without review.
99	- Remediation:
100	  - Require the panel to have seen no key for a quiet period (e.g. 600-800 ms of no input after first draw) before
101	    any decision key is armed. Keys during the unarmed period reset the timer and show "keys ignored, pause to decide".
102	  - Make `a` a two-step confirmation (`a` then `y`/Enter on a confirm row), or move it behind ←/→ plus Enter.
103	  - Default focus to Deny (or no focus, so Enter does nothing until an arrow key is pressed).
104	  - Optionally require uppercase or modifier keys for approve.
105	- Acceptance test: A unit test feeds the steering string at 120-200 ms per key, starting 300 ms before the panel is
106	  shown, and expects no `Approve`/`Deny` and the panel still open. A PTY variant of tui_approval_driver.py does the
107	  same with `os.write` per key at 150 ms, then expects decisions == [] and the file not written.
108	- Dependencies: none. Not addressed by any commit on feat/tui-surface (804c5df handles queued input, bursts and pastes only).
109	
110	### F2 An approval can be decided while the panel is not on screen (terminal below 40x10)
111	- Priority: P2
112	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT (unit level)
113	- Affects: main, feat/tui-surface, installed runtime
114	- Trigger: The terminal is smaller than MIN_WIDTH x MIN_HEIGHT (40x10) when an approval arrives (split pane, tmux
115	  pane, resized window).
116	- Expected: No decision is possible until the panel, including the change, has been visible.
117	- Observed: `render_live` (804c5df live_view.rs:98-103) draws only "Nexus needs a larger terminal (40×10 minimum).",
118	  but `draw()` → `note_layout` (live_state.rs:1094-1096) calls `note_approval_shown(Instant::now())`
119	  unconditionally. Probe `live_view::review_small::review_small_screens` prints

121	  exactly 40x10 the panel is "shown" with zero diff rows visible (screen dump in Visual defects).
122	- Impact: The operator approves a change they never saw, contradicting the 804c5df claim "no decision before the
123	  panel has been drawn".
124	- Remediation: Have `render_approval` return whether the subject and at least one change row (or the whole change)
125	  were drawn, put that in `LiveLayout` (e.g. `approval_visible: bool`), and call `note_approval_shown` only when it

129	  either at least one diff row is visible or decisions stay disarmed.

132	### F3 An approval replaces whatever panel is open; the key meant for that panel decides
133	- Priority: P2
134	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT (unit level)
135	- Affects: main, feat/tui-surface
136	- Trigger: Help, the diff review, the models picker or the provider connect panel is open when an approval arrives.

content.text:
I've reconciled the other agent's work with mine and found and fixed a performance regression in it. Three things are running in the background:
- the PTY reliability runs on the TUI-only build: 1 of 13 done and passing; the 10 serial runs plus 3 under load take about an hour;
- the independent review of the other agent's stages 0–5;
- nothing is committed yet.

**Done since your last message**
- **Resumed sessions (O3):** the resumed view now lists the tools the agent called and how the last turn ended.
- **Remaining visual defects** from the independent review:
  - the help panel shows a scroll indicator and the visible row range;
  - narrow diffs wrap between words instead of mid-word;
  - the crash screen no longer adds "(no exit code)" after a signal, and drops log lines left over from finished turns;
  - the evidence script now captures the real tool-detail panel.
- **Two TUI clippy warnings fixed.** The `harness-core` warnings already existed at `ba2c4ef`.
- **The other agent's polish reviewed and kept:** command output now shows its last lines, long lines at 40 columns end in `…`, and the approval decision appears before its result. I fixed one bug in it: the help position counter wasn't clamped to the scroll range.
- **One reported defect didn't reproduce:** the "wrapped code row loses its background". The screen data and the PNG pixels both show the background.
- **Every change has a test**, and each new test fails without its change.

**Found while verifying**
- **A 5× slowdown in the other agent's secret redaction.** It read every environment variable once for each string it scanned, about 8,000 times per pass. A 35-step turn went from 19.8 s to 111 s and timed out under load. It now reads the environment once per pass, and a regression test covers it.
- **My assessment commit broke `make test` on this branch and on main (`c7234bb`).** The security gate's secret scan matched two synthetic fixture strings (`sk-assessfake…`, `ghp_ABCD…`) in the review repro tests. They aren't real secrets. The other agent had stopped the scan from failing by excluding all of `docs/reviews/`, which would also miss a real key pasted into a review. I narrowed the exclusion to the repro fixture folders; the review documents are scanned again.
- **10 CLI test failures in the combined tree, all from stages 1, 3 and 5.**
  - **Parser test: fixed.** Model reasoning is now kept separate from the reply. I also made sure it's still written to the flight log, which the change had dropped.
  - **Not yet fixed, waiting on the review:**
    - Seven failures come from the new "regression-free, not verified" rule. The tests assert the old meaning, where a passing generic `make test` counts as verified. The rule that decides "these tests cover the change" is a weak name match and rescans the whole workspace every turn.
    - Two doctor failures come from the new trust gate. A project's `.mcp.json` and plugins are now silently ignored unless the workspace is trusted, and nothing in Nexus can grant trust. The only ways are `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1` or editing `~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json` by hand.

**How I'll commit**
- The TUI work and the qualification stages are separate features, so they get separate commits on `feat/tui-surface`.
- First, the security-gate fix on its own.
- Then the TUI work, checked by itself in a clean worktree. There `make test` passes completely: 728 CLI tests, 228 TUI tests and all PTY scenarios.
- The stage 0–5 work stays uncommitted until the failures above are resolved.
- When the PTY runs finish, I'll make both commits, re-capture the evidence from the TUI commit, and hand the visuals and approval behaviour to an independent reviewer.

**Needs your decision**
- Main has the same security-gate failure from `c7234bb`. I can cherry-pick the gate fix to main in a temporary worktree. Say if you want that.

I ran `cargo test` on the base commit plus the changed Rust files. It passed with 220 unit tests and the integration tests. Several TS suites fail on the changed code (listed under "Tests run" below). An earlier baseline log in the scratchpad (`base_npm.log`) shows 2 failures, both `security_gates` and environmental.

## Findings, ranked

1. **BLOCKER – `core/src/file_ops.rs` (`edit_file`, `delete_file`) vs `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts:467–490` and the `edit_file` schema (~268–295): the new arguments are not in the tool schemas.**
   - `delete_file` now refuses directories unless `recursive=true`, and the model-facing schema has no `recursive` parameter. Its description still says "Delete a file or directory". Directory deletion is therefore unreachable for schema-following models.
   - `edit_file` returns "set replace_all: true" on ambiguous matches, but `replace_all` is not in the schema either.
   - Fix: add both parameters to the schemas, or make the error text not mention parameters the model cannot see.
   - `docs/USER_MANUAL.md:217` still says "fuzzy recovery".

2. **BLOCKER – `cli/src/tester.ts:24–31`: the test-filter sanitizer allows newlines, so the cargo path still injects commands.**
   - The allowlist includes `\s`, which matches `\n` and `\r`.
   - Reproduced: `detectTestCommand(<Cargo.toml dir>, "foo\ntouch /tmp/pwned")` returns `cargo test -- foo\ntouch /tmp/pwned`. The cargo branches (lines 45 and 49) interpolate the filter unquoted.
   - Fix: replace `\s` with a literal space, `[A-Za-z0-9_:./ -]`. Also forbid a leading `-` so a filter cannot become a flag.

3. **BLOCKER – `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts:787`: `run_tests` is now `mutating: true`.**
   - `cli/src/core/spine.ts:575` treats any successful mutating capability as `candidateMutated`.
   - The `candidateMutation` hook at `cli/src/agent.ts:743–752` then runs `mutationSeq++`, `invalidateVerified`, `setUnverifiedChanges(true)`, clears `verificationEvidence`, and increments `turnMutations`.
   - So a model-invoked passing `run_tests` demotes verified requirements and marks the turn as having unverified changes. A test-only turn can no longer end as `NOT_REQUIRED`.
   - I found this by reading the code and did not run a probe.
   - It also makes `run_tests` prompt for approval, because `agent.ts:2574` now uses `cap.mutating`.
   - Fix: keep `mutating: true` for the read-only gate only. Add a separate flag (for example `mutatesCandidate: false`) that the spine uses for `candidateMutated`. Alternatively, exempt `test_discover_run` the way `orchestration` is exempted at line 744.

4. **BLOCKER (test suite) – five existing tests fail and were not updated.**
   - `turn_semantics.test.ts:242` and `:257` expect VERIFIED and get REGRESSION_FREE.
   - `turn_semantics.test.ts:573` expects exit 0 and gets 2.
   - `convergence_invariants.test.ts:179` and `:303` fail the same way. At `:303` the subagent reports "REGRESSION_FREE: Passing test run did not cover the modified deliverables."
   - Those fixtures use a trivial verifier such as `true`, so the downgrade is working as designed. The tests and the "verifier must name the deliverable" contract need an explicit decision.
   - `doctor.test.ts:251` ("MCP servers and plugins are inspected…") also fails: it expects `warn` and gets `skip`. `doctor` now ignores workspace `.mcp.json` and plugins because they are untrusted.
   - Fix: update the tests, and let `doctor` report the untrusted workspace config as a finding instead of skipping it.

5. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/agent.ts:653,1273` and `cli/src/plugins.ts`: the read-only plugin gate is not wired.**
   - `new PluginManager(ws)` is called without `readOnly`, and `isWorkspaceTrusted(ws, false)` is used. A trusted workspace therefore still loads plugins under `--read-only`.
   - `McpClientManager` does receive `readOnly`, so the summary's "disables them in --read-only" holds for MCP only.
   - Fix: pass `{ readOnly: config.readOnly }` at both sites.

6. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/workspace_trust.ts`: nothing can grant trust.**
   - `setWorkspaceTrusted` has no caller and there is no CLI or slash command for it. The only paths are the `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1` environment variable or hand-editing `~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json`.
   - Workspace plugins and `.mcp.json` are now silently dead, with no prompt and no diagnostic, so this is a regression for existing users.
   - The trust file is also writable by the agent's own `run_command`, unless it is a protected path.
   - Fix: add `nexus trust [path]` with a warning when an untrusted config is skipped. Add `~/.config/nexus` to `isPathProtected`.

7. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/tester.ts:236–290` (`isVerifierDeliverableBound`) is both too strict and too loose.**
   - Too strict:
     - Rust inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests never count. For a change to `file_ops.rs` with `cargo test`, the command does not name the file and there is no `*_test` file, so the result is REGRESSION_FREE forever.
     - A root-level `test_foo.py` is not matched by `isTestPath`.
     - Non-test verifiers such as `tsc --noEmit`, a build, or `./check.sh` always downgrade.
   - Too loose:
     - Step 3 returns true if any test file contains the changed file's stem. A common stem such as `index`, `agent` or `utils` almost always matches.
     - Steps 2 and 3 never check that the matching test actually ran.
   - Cost: step 3 does a synchronous read of every test file, up to depth 4 with no size cap, per verification and per `run_tests` call.
   - Fix: bind on the output evidence (test names or paths reported as run) plus an explicit allowance for ecosystems with inline tests. Cache the scan and bound it by size.

8. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/tester.ts:200–204`: `isFilteredVerifierCommand` and `hasExecutedTests` have gaps and false positives.**
   - Not detected as filtered: `go test -run=X`, `node --test --test-name-pattern=x`, `make test FILTER=foo` (the pattern needs trailing whitespace), `pytest a.py::test_b`, and positional `cargo test name`.
   - False positive: `git diff -- src` is flagged as filtered.
   - `hasExecutedTests` returns true for `0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 12 filtered out`.
   - Fix: match `-run[= ]`, `--test-name-pattern`, `FILTER=\S`, `::`, and positional arguments for known runners. For the zero-pass case, require `passed > 0`.

9. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/core/egress.ts:~238`: the broadened generic secret regex redacts ordinary code.**
   - It now allows an optional opening quote and a bare `auth`. I measured these:
     - `password = process.env.DB_PASSWORD` classifies `process.env.DB_PASSWORD`.
     - `secret = os.environ["X"]` classifies `os.environ[`.
     - `auth = require("./auth")` classifies `require(`.
     - `password: Optional[str]` classifies `Optional[str]`.
     - `self.auth_token = REDACTED classifies `self._generate_token()`.
   - Each matched value is then `replaceAll`'d over the whole text, which corrupts code shown to the model and in telemetry.
   - It also raises false quarantines on `search_web` and `fetch_web`.
   - Fix: restore the required quote, or require the value to contain no `(`, `[`, `.` or `)` unless quoted. Drop bare `auth`.
   - The new environment-variable secrets have the same flaw: any value of 8+ characters in a variable whose name contains `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` and similar is replaced everywhere. Add a minimum length of about 16, exclude path-like values, and skip common words.

10. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/ui.ts:6–15` with `cli/src/sidecar.ts:338`: `redactSecrets` is now heavy and runs per streamed delta.**
    - It runs the full `redactForTelemetry` pipeline (environment enumeration, a pass over all patterns, and entropy tokenization) for each `assistant.delta`.
    - I measured about 0.4 ms per call, on a 96-variable environment under load. Note that `sidecar.ts` is outside the stated scope.
    - Fix: for deltas, keep the cheap regex-only path and redact fully at message end.
    - Deltas also split tokens, so full redaction per delta gives weaker protection anyway.

11. **SHOULD-FIX – `core/src/runner.rs:214–235`: bounded drain discards all output on timeout.**
    - If a reader does not finish within 500 ms, for example because a backgrounded `server &` holds the pipe, `Vec::new()` replaces the whole stdout or stderr. Everything already read is lost.
    - It also calls `terminate_process_tree`, which adds up to 500 ms of SIGTERM grace and kills the daemon.
    - `drain_timeout` can be 0 when `remaining_time` is 0, which loses output from a command that finished right at the limit.
    - Fix: have the reader threads share an `Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>` and return whatever has been collected. Compute the drain as a floor, not `min(remaining, 500ms)`.

12. **SHOULD-FIX – `core/src/file_ops.rs:89–154` (`write_file_atomically`): several behaviours change.**
    - **Cleanup:** the temp file is not removed if `verify_descriptor_confinement` or `write_all` fails, which leaves `.name.tmp_atomic.<ns>` files in the workspace.
    - **Read-only files:** a file with mode 0444 in a writable directory can now be edited. The old in-place open failed. Check `meta.permissions().readonly()` first.
    - **Metadata:** ownership, ACLs, xattrs and hard links are not preserved.
    - **Race:** `create_dir_all` runs before the jail check on the parent, so directories can be created outside the jail. The check precedes the mkdir only in `write_file`'s earlier pre-check, which does not cover this path.
    - **Permission window:** `set_permissions` is applied after the content is written, so a restrictive mode is applied late.
    - **Temp name:** it uses a timestamp only. Add a counter or random suffix.

13. **SHOULD-FIX – `core/src/file_ops.rs:~610–650` (`edit_file`): "exact match only" is not what is implemented.**
    - The trim fallback, `norm_orig.contains(trimmed_old)`, still matches sub-token substrings. `old="x = 1\n"` matches inside `x = 10`, and the result becomes `x = 20`.
    - `line_by_line_trim_match` ignores indentation, and the replacement uses the model's indentation.
    - In a file with mixed endings, `has_crlf` converts every `\n` to `\r\n`, including untouched LF lines.
    - The exact-match branch inserts a bare `\n` into a CRLF file when the match is single-line but the replacement is multi-line.
    - Fix: require line boundaries for the trimmed match, and normalise line endings per line.

14. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/core/authority.ts:~128` and `cli/src/tools.ts:~482`: the `--pre` check is not applied in the bridge's read-only gate.**
    - Authority uses `isSafeReadOnlyCommand`, but the bridge's read-only enforcement still uses `SAFE_READONLY_COMMAND_REGEX.test`. Only dry-run was switched to the new function.
    - Fix: use the same function in both places.
    - The check also misses `rg --hostname-bin`, which executes a program.

15. **SHOULD-FIX – `cli/src/security.ts:~230`: the vault restore fails closed only when `isAuthorizedSink === false` is passed.**
    - An omitted context still rehydrates. The only caller found, `agent.ts:2503`, passes `true` explicitly.
    - Fix: invert the default so restore requires an explicit `true`.

16. **SHOULD-FIX – `.gitlab-ci.yml`: the pipeline cannot work as written.**
    - The `node:20-bookworm` image has no Rust toolchain, and `make build` runs `cargo build`.
    - `npm install` is never run, and `node_modules` is not an artifact, so the `test` stage has no dependencies.
    - Fix: use an image with both toolchains, or add a Rust setup step, and add `npm ci` plus a cache.

17. **NIT – `cli/src/build_identity.ts` and `cli/src/index.ts:65`: startup cost and a missing field.**
    - The summary said "build time", but no build timestamp is recorded.
    - `getBuildIdentity()` runs at module load, so two `execSync` git calls happen on every `harness` start, including the sidecar and `doctor`.
    - `dirty` is evaluated at runtime, and `cli/dist` is tracked, so a rebuilt install always reports dirty.
    - Fix: bake the identity at build time into `build_identity.json` and only fall back to git lazily.

18. **NIT – `cli/src/mcp.ts:49–70` (`buildMcpEnvironment`): the environment scrub is too aggressive.**
    - Proxy variables, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are dropped, which breaks MCP servers behind proxies or custom CAs.
    - Fix: add an allow-extension setting, or document it.

19. **NIT – `cli/src/tools.ts:458` and `agent.ts:2511`: duplicated deletion guards, and `.git` internals are deletable.**
    - The same check exists in the bridge, the agent and Rust.
    - Deleting `.git/objects` or `.git/HEAD` with `recursive` is still allowed.
    - Fix: guard any path with a `.git` component, and remove the duplicates.

20. **NIT – `core/src/runner.rs:42–60`: the truncation byte count is correct but the tail loop is awkward.** Prefer `floor_char_boundary` or `ceil_char_boundary` when available.

## 4. Safety, Compliance & Resilience

- **Workspace Symlink Boundary Confinement**: Native Rust canonicalization verifies that neither relative paths nor symlinks can escape the workspace jail directory.
- **Configurable Security Policy (`.nexus-security.json`)**: Declare repository-specific blocked shell commands, protected files (`.git`, `.env`, keys), and allowed outbound network domains.
- **Dry-Run & Read-Only Modes**:
  - `--dry-run`: Intercepts file writes and mutating commands to simulate changes without touching disk.
  - `--read-only`: Rejects all file modifications and non-read shell commands with an immediate error.
- **Lightweight Container Sandboxing (`--sandbox`)**: Restricts filesystem mutation strictly to the target workspace using Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker isolation.
- **Worker Thread Plugin Sandboxing**: Untrusted or custom plugin handlers execute in isolated Node.js `worker_threads` with strict timeout boundaries and memory caps.
- **Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) Allocation**: Commands requiring TTY capabilities run inside allocated virtual pseudo-terminals via `portable-pty`.
- **Multi-Provider Failover**: Specify secondary fallback endpoints via `--fallback <url1,url2>` or `$LOCAL_LLM_FALLBACK_ENDPOINTS`. Automatic failover occurs if the primary LLM server drops connection or runs out of GPU VRAM (HTTP 503).
- **BPE Token Accounting & Context Gauge**: Real-time token breakdown across system instructions, tools schema, user messages, assistant thinking, and tool output payloads with visual ANSI progress gauge.
- **Structured Context Compaction**: `/compact` distills discarded messages into structured memory (files touched, commands run, architectural decisions) instead of discarding context blindly.
- **Dynamic Few-Shot Injection**: Context-aware injection of valid tool exemplars (edits, test repair, batch reads) tailored to the active task, eliminating tool hallucination in local models (Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek Coder).
- **Dangerous Command Guard**: Blocks destructive commands (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, raw device writes, fork bombs) from executing.
- **SSRF Network Protection**: Blocks outbound access to loopback (`127.0.0.1`), cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`), and private RFC-1918 subnets in `fetch_web`.
- **Non-Blocking Pipe Execution**: Drains stdout and stderr concurrently to prevent 64KB Linux buffer saturation deadlocks during intensive builds.
- **Secret Redaction**: Redacts Bearer tokens, private keys, and passwords before printing or logging.
- **Audit Logging**: Every tool execution is recorded with timestamps, parameters, duration, and status in `~/.nexus/audit.log`. Visual inspection available via `/audit` and `nexus audit`.
- **Workspace Snapshots & Rollback**: Automatic Git-backed and filesystem snapshot rollback. Inspect diffs anytime with `/checkpoint diff <id>`, and manage disk footprint with `/checkpoint prune [keep]`.
- **Real-Time Hot-Reloading**: Automatically detects edits or additions in `skills/` and `AGENTS.md` and reloads them dynamically without restarting the REPL.

Stages 0–5 of the top-tier qualification assessment (implemented by a

change — tests executed (runner counts), the whole suite (no name filter),
and coverage of the changed files (a changed test, the run naming a changed
file, a test importing a changed module, or inline Rust/Go tests); an
operator-configured verifier counts as the operator's acceptance check.

requirements cannot be marked verified. run_tests returns a bounded report
and is not a workspace change (new `changesWorkspace` capability flag).

Execution authority and trust: read-only blocks mutating capabilities in the
bridge with the authority engine's command check (rg --pre/--hostname-bin
refused); plugins and MCP honour --read-only; workspace .mcp.json and plugins
load only for trusted workspaces (`nexus trust`, notices, doctor findings;
trust store protected); test filters cannot inject commands; the workspace

The last re-acceptance round found that, after a pause in typing, cursor keys (→ → Enter, ← ← Enter) or Ctrl+A then Enter could approve all later actions. It also found that Ctrl/Alt combinations counted as `y`/`n`/`a` answers. The fixes:

- **Arrow choices:** Enter takes one only right after it, once it has been on screen for 400 ms. The choice doesn't wrap around, and Tab (slash-command completion) never chooses.
- **Ctrl/Alt combinations** never answer the panel.
- **Draft in the composer:** the `y`/`n`/`a` shortcuts are off while you have a draft. A panel you typed into keeps them off, even after a resize.
- **Small fixes:**
  - scrolling the change keeps your choice;
  - letter shortcuts are hidden on the buttons when they're off;
  - Esc denies when the terminal is too small to draw the panel;
  - approvals that arrive while a panel is open wait in order instead of replacing each other.

Every case the reviewer reproduced is now a unit or PTY regression test.

- `make test`: Rust 24 + 235 + 2, CLI 810/810, security gates pass. No clippy warnings in the TUI.

Round 4 again did **not** accept approval safety. With pauses of 400 ms or more, `→ → Enter Enter` still approves all later actions (PTY 3 of 3). Smaller issues:

Four rounds in, the pattern is clear: as long as arrows and Enter (keys every typist uses on a draft) can reach "approve all later actions", timing thresholds just move the hole around. So I'm re-planning rather than tuning again:
1. **Approve all later actions** is reachable only through `a` on a panel whose letters are armed, followed by two Enters. Arrows only ever choose between Approve and Deny.
2. **On a panel that was typed into or opened over a draft,** an arrow choice must stay on screen for 2 s before Enter takes it (400 ms on an armed panel).
3. **Modifiers:** arrows and Enter count only with no modifiers; letters allow Shift only. No Ctrl, Alt, Super, Meta or Hyper.
4. **Confirm step:** Enter confirms, Esc denies, any other key only cancels it.
5. **A panel drawn right after a decision** (within 2 s) starts with letters off and shows how many approvals are waiting.
6. **Selecting a choice isn't typing**, so `a` then Enter doesn't trip the quiet period. The help overlay will match.

# Evaluation harness (qualification assessment §9)

`run.mjs` runs tasks against one agent configuration and appends a JSON line per run; `score.mjs` reports the scores
separately (never combined), per task and configuration, with 95 % Wilson intervals.

```bash
node eval/run.mjs --config eval/configs/gateway-engineering-deep.json --out eval/out/<label> [--only id,id] [--runs N]
node eval/score.mjs eval/out/<label>/results.jsonl          # markdown table; --json for machine output
```

Each run: a fresh workspace (the task's `fixture`, or its `repo.url` at `repo.commit`, cached in `eval/.cache`), a fresh
`HOME`, the agent with the task's budgets and a wall-clock timeout, then the task's **hidden** tests (copied in only
after the agent has stopped) and its `regression` command. `manifest.json` records the harness build (commit, dirty),
the configuration (secrets in `env` masked), host and Node version; per-run logs go to `logs/<task>-<run>/`.

## Task format (`eval/tasks/<id>/task.json`)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id`, `tier` | T1 smoke (scripted model, CI), T2 standard, T3 long-task, T4 fault-injected |
| `fixture` or `repo` | a directory in the task, or `{ "url", "commit" }` (external repositories at pinned commits) |
| `setup` | shell commands run in the workspace before the agent (e.g. `npm ci`) |
| `objective` | the operator text given to the agent |
| `steps`, `minutes` | budgets (defaults from the configuration: 300 steps, 120 min) |
| `hidden` | `{ dir, into, command, timeoutSec }` — tests the agent never sees; pass = artifact correct |
| `regression` | `{ command }` — the repository's own suite after the run |

## Scores

completion claimed · artifact correct (hidden tests) · false VERIFIED (VERIFIED while hidden tests fail) · regressions
introduced · timed out / harness errors · wall time, steps, tokens (median). Context qualifier (`contextNotRetained`) is
recorded per run.

## Pre-registered thresholds (from the assessment, fixed before any live run)

- false VERIFIED = 0 across all runs;
- T2 hidden-test pass rate ≥ best matched peer on the same local model minus a margin — **margin not yet fixed**
  (to be recorded here before the first live run), or an absolute target if no peer can be matched;
- T3: false-absence claims = 0 and steering constraints honoured in ≥ 95 % of runs;
- T4: truthful bounded outcome in 100 % of fault runs;
- ≥ 5 runs per task-configuration, per-task results with 95 % intervals.

| Part | State |
|---|---|

| T1 self-test (`selftest-add`, scripted model, in `make test` via `cli/test/eval_harness.test.ts`) | done |

| T3 fact-sheet scorer (absence claims) and steering checks | not started |
| T4 fault injector | not started |
| Live runs | blocked on inference hours, cloud budget and peer installs (operator decision) |
EOF
